scope: Phase 1 private notes critical vertical spike

dataInventory.retention: until the synthetic fixture is reset; no production or customer data
dataInventory.backup: isolated E2E backend backup policy only; no device cache or application backup

dataInventory.retention: session lifetime and provider refresh policy
dataInventory.backup: must follow platform secure-storage rules and never be copied into application backup or evidence

protectAgainst: accidental plaintext leakage through app logs, crash reports, analytics, screenshots, recordings, clipboard, AsyncStorage, caches, files, or committed evidence
lost device storage access within the guarantees of iOS Keychain and Android Keystore-backed storage
stolen backend media or backup within the hosted provider encryption boundary
trustedPlaintextProcessors: the authorized installed mobile application while rendering or editing a note
Supabase Auth/API/Postgres processes and explicitly authorized project operators
explicitlyNotProtectedAgainst: a compromised or malicious privileged Supabase/backend operator
a fully compromised unlocked device or hostile code running in the application process
legal or provider access inside the trusted hosted-service boundary

decision.rationale: Use P0 for note content in the isolated spike and P1 for authentication credentials. This proves authorization, native lifecycle, plaintext-sink discipline, and platform secure storage without introducing an unvalidated backend encryption service or E2EE recovery product into the first vertical slice.
rejectedAlternatives: P2 server envelope encryption is deferred because it would replace direct client-to-Supabase protected-field writes with a trusted encryption service and KMS, materially expanding Phase 1 infrastructure.
P3 client E2EE is deferred because multi-device recovery, lost-device behavior, sharing, search, support, and key ownership are unresolved product decisions.
Supabase Vault is not used for note fields because its decrypted view remains plaintext-accessible to authorized database roles and does not provide E2EE.

controls.transport: TLS required for every mobile-to-Supabase request; no plaintext endpoints
controls.authorization: RLS owner equality and cross-user denial remain mandatory independently of encryption
controls.localStorage: session credentials only in the version-matched platform-protected store; note title/body never persisted in AsyncStorage, SQLite, files, query persistence, or offline queues
controls.remoteStorage: note content remains plaintext to authorized Supabase processing and encrypted only by provider-managed at-rest controls
controls.logsAndTelemetry: note title/body, tokens, email fixtures, and authorization headers are redacted from app, Metro, native, backend, crash, analytics, CI, and agent evidence
controls.backup: no note content in app backup; platform-protected credential entries follow verified iOS/Android semantics; E2E backend retention is temporary and fixture-owned
controls.clipboardAndScreenshots: the feature provides no copy action; test screenshots use synthetic known content and are retained only as redacted run evidence

cryptography.library: version-matched Expo SecureStore adapter for session persistence plus hosted platform controls; exact version selected after H1 from installed Expo SDK

classes.owner: iOS or Android platform security subsystem
classes.location: system-managed protection used by the version-matched SecureStore adapter
hosted provider storage boundary; metadata only visible to agents

keyLifecycle.generation: delegated to Supabase Auth, iOS/Android platform storage, and hosted storage controls
keyLifecycle.storage: no application-owned DEK or KEK; agents record metadata only
keyLifecycle.rotation: session rotation follows Auth; provider-managed at-rest key rotation is outside the spike and must not be inferred
keyLifecycle.revocation: logout/revoked session deletes local credentials and denies API access
keyLifecycle.recovery: a missing or invalidated local session requires re-authentication; note data remains server-recoverable because Phase 1 is not E2EE
keyLifecycle.deletion: fixture reset deletes notes; logout removes session material; no cryptographic erasure claim

platformBehavior.ios: verify Keychain-backed session persistence, accessibility choice, logout deletion, and observed reinstall behavior on the selected release-like build
platformBehavior.android: verify Keystore-backed session persistence, logout deletion, and SecureStore exclusion from Android Auto Backup
platformBehavior.reinstall: the app must tolerate missing credentials and require login; it must not promise identical iOS and Android persistence semantics
platformBehavior.biometricChange: biometric-gated access is not required in Phase 1; if added, return to H1 and test invalidation on a physical device

requiredEvidence: dependency/config review proving a version-matched secure-storage adapter and Android backup exclusion
static scan proving no server keys, raw cryptographic keys, credentials, note content, or authorization headers in bundle/config/log fixtures
unit/integration evidence for session adapter failure, logout deletion, RLS denial, and TLS-only endpoints
known-marker scan of AsyncStorage, SQLite, application files, logs, crash/analytics payloads, screenshots metadata, and committed evidence
native iOS and Android replay for restart, logout/re-authentication, offline error, and absence of unintended note persistence
backend oracle proving cross-user denial and documenting that authorized Postgres storage contains plaintext note content under the accepted P0 boundary
operator review of residual privileged plaintext access at H1 and H2
residualRisks: authorized Supabase/backend processes and privileged operators can read note content
a fully compromised unlocked device or app process can observe rendered plaintext and session use
simulator/emulator evidence cannot prove physical-device biometric or hardware-backed key properties
provider-managed storage encryption and rotation are attested platform controls rather than application-layer evidence
